title: TradingView Visual Oracle — released-build parity manifest (v2, split logic / feed / production-replay parity)
description: Committed record of ONE released Pine build: exactly which production behaviour it mirrors, which stages were validated ALONG WHICH PARITY DIMENSION, and what it is known not to do. Written by the update workflow, read by tools/oracle/check_freshness.py. Location: artifacts/tradingview_oracle/parity_manifest.json. This file is the ONLY authority on whether a released chart is current — never a timestamp, never a commit message. v2 replaces v1's single overloaded per-stage status with four independent dimensions, because one string could not distinguish 'the Pine is a faithful port' from 'the broker's feed matches production'. A v1 manifest is migrated fail-closed: a legacy MATCHED is NOT carried into any dimension (see tools/oracle/parity_status.py::migrate_stage_record).

oracle_version.description: Semver of the Pine oracle build itself, independent of the engine it mirrors.

generated_at.description: UTC ISO-8601. Provenance only — never used for freshness.

fingerprint.description: Verbatim copy of the contract's fingerprint block. `inputs` is what check_freshness compares field by field.

oracle_engine_id.description: Human-readable HUD label. NEVER a comparison key.

production.description: Provenance of the tree the build was generated from. Recorded for humans; the fingerprint is what gates.

pine_source.description: The generated artefact. `sha256` is line-ending normalised, so a Windows/macOS checkout of the same content agrees. A mismatch means the generated file was HAND-EDITED and is reported as INCOMPATIBLE.

module_sources.description: The structured fragments the artefact was assembled from, in assembly order.

supported_context.description: A chart outside this is UNSUPPORTED_DATA_CONTEXT — the oracle must say so rather than render a plausible wrong answer.

minimum_history_bars.description: Below these depths the history-seeded values (ATR RMA seed, swing_trend_bias, regime panel) have not converged and parity is meaningless.

stages.description: Per-stage parity record keyed by the Phase 0 audit section 18 stage ids (S1..S14). Each stage carries FOUR independent statuses. A passing early stage must never imply whole-engine parity, and a passing LOGIC parity must never imply the chart reproduces production's numbers.

implementation_status.description: Does the released Pine contain this stage at all? Never a statement about correctness.

logic_parity.description: Given the SAME ordered bars and the same declared initialisation, does Pine reproduce the Python algorithm? The ONLY dimension a Pine defect can move, and the only one a chart_bars comparison can establish.

input_basis.description: MUST be chart_bars for any matched status: a fixture_bars divergence may be the feed.

bootstrap_bars.description: Declared initialisation interval excluded from scoring. Required and positive for LOGIC_MATCHED_WITH_DECLARED_BOOTSTRAP.

bootstrap_window.description: [first, last] UTC bar of the excluded interval. An unbounded bootstrap is not a declared one.

post_bootstrap_divergences.description: Divergences AFTER the declared interval. Must be 0 for any matched status — a recurring divergence is not a seed.

build_fingerprint.description: The build fingerprint this evidence was gathered against. Freshness compares it to the current build so evidence cannot silently outlive what it measured.

superseded.description: A claim demoted because its build fingerprint no longer matches. Kept so the demotion is auditable and so a refresh can be seen to restore what was lost.

feed_parity.description: Does the TradingView feed deliver the same bars as production? A property of the DATA. No Pine change can move it.

production_replay_parity.description: Does Pine reproduce the exact historical production trace — production feed, production seed, full history? Presupposes logic parity AND feed parity.

reason.description: Required when the status is REPLAY_UNATTAINABLE_IN_CURRENT_CONTEXT.

build_fingerprint.description: The build fingerprint this evidence was gathered against. Freshness compares it to the current build so evidence cannot silently outlive what it measured.

superseded.description: A claim demoted because its build fingerprint no longer matches. Kept so the demotion is auditable and so a refresh can be seen to restore what was lost.

migrated_from.description: Present only on a stage carried over from a v1 manifest. Records the legacy claim that was DISCARDED, so the downgrade is auditable rather than silent.

global_status.description: Derived, never hand-set. MATCHED requires EVERY stage to be implemented AND logic-matched AND feed-matched AND replay-matched — a strictly stronger claim than v1's MATCHED, and unreachable on a feed that differs from production's. INCOMPATIBLE if any unsupported feature is active or the Pine source hash mismatches; STALE if the engine moved; PARTIAL if any stage is unimplemented or any dimension is unproven; UNVERIFIED if never validated.

tested_windows.description: The data windows parity was actually measured over. A claim outside a tested window is not evidence.

golden_fixtures.description: Content hashes of the trace fixtures this build was validated against. A changed hash means the baseline moved and the stage must be re-validated.

known_limitations.description: Limitation ids from audit section 12 that are ACTIVE for this build, with the approximation actually shipped.

measured_divergence.description: Populated once a fixture has actually measured it. null means the expectation is still unverified.

unsupported_active_features.description: MUST be empty for a compatible build. A non-empty list forces global_status INCOMPATIBLE: a production mechanism the oracle does not implement is live.

enum_coverage.description: Proof that every production enum value has a Pine mapping. `unmapped` MUST be empty — an unmapped value would render as a generic state, which is exactly what the design forbids.

feed_measurement.description: The measured difference between the production dataset and the charted feed. Carried once and referenced by every stage's feed_parity. This is the evidence behind FEED_DIFFERENT; without it the status is an opinion.
